blocks.heading: “Balance is the only quest,” Shiva said to himself. And then he asked, *“Why is it so difficult to attain?”*
He took a deep breath, a faint, knowing smile upon His face.

blocks.leftColumn: “The reasons are many. What burdens one may not burden another. Some will blame the physical world; some, the unseen realms of being. Some will call it a pursuit of right, others a surrender to wrong.
blocks.rightColumn: But what one calls right must always be someone else’s wrong. What they fail to understand is this — nothing is absolutely right, and nothing is absolutely wrong.”

blocks.heading: Yet there must be a reason, for the quest itself is Balance.

*He asks:* “What is the void to be filled? What is the cure to this chaos?”

*He replies:* “Knowledge is the cure. And therefore, the void is ignorance.”

So ignorance must dissolve, and knowledge must prevail.

But then He wondered — “If knowledge alone prevails, will balance remain? Will nature, creation, space, and time become too still… too static?”
